title: Number Quest Unit 2 · The Cold Store (Pro)

items.q: A pot holds 6 liters. Each jar holds 3/4 of a liter. How many jars can be filled?
misconceptions: multiplied 6 by 3/4 instead of dividing
correct
multiplied by 4 but forgot to divide by 3
divided by 3 and ignored the fourths
items.why: Each liter is 4 fourths, so 6 liters are 24 fourths. Jars of 3 fourths: 24 ÷ 3 = 8. Check: 8 × 3/4 = 6.

items.q: Which multiplication gives the same answer as 5 ÷ 2/3?
misconceptions: correct
kept the divisor as it was instead of using its reciprocal
flipped the dividend instead of the divisor
flipped both numbers, not only the divisor
items.why: Dividing by a fraction is multiplying by its reciprocal. Only the divisor turns over: 5 ÷ 2/3 = 5 × 3/2 = 15/2 = 7 1/2.

items.q: You have 1/2 of a liter. A jar holds 3/4 of a liter. What fraction of the jar is filled?
misconceptions: multiplied the two fractions instead of dividing
divided 3/4 by 1/2, the wrong way round
correct
subtracted 1/2 from 3/4 instead of dividing
items.why: 1/2 ÷ 3/4 = 1/2 × 4/3 = 4/6 = 2/3. The jar holds more than you have, so it must be less than full.

items.q: A diver is 12 meters below sea level and a bird is 9 meters above it. Sea level is 0. Which pair of numbers shows the two positions?
misconceptions: correct
swapped which side of zero is negative
ignored that below sea level is negative
made both numbers negative
items.why: Sea level is zero. Below it is negative and above it is positive, so the diver is at −12 meters and the bird is at 9 meters.

items.q: What is the opposite of the opposite of −4?
misconceptions: stopped after taking the opposite once
correct
added the number to its opposite
doubled the number instead of reflecting it twice
items.why: The opposite of −4 is 4, and the opposite of 4 is −4. Taking the opposite twice always returns the number you started with.

items.q: Three freezers read −15°C, −9°C and 12°C. Which statement puts the readings in order?
misconceptions: compared 9 and 15 and ignored the negative signs
correct
ordered the readings by their distance from zero
wrote the order from greatest to least
items.why: Lower on the thermometer is less. −15 is below −9, and both are below 12, so −15 < −9 < 12. The coldest reading is the least number.

items.q: A sample is at −6°C. What change brings it to 4°C?
misconceptions: subtracted 4 from 6 instead of adding the two distances
gave the right size with the wrong direction
correct
added −6 and 4 instead of finding the change between them
items.why: From −6 it takes 6 steps up to reach zero and 4 more to reach 4, so the change is +10. Check: −6 + 10 = 4.

misconceptions: correct
dropped the negative sign of the number being subtracted
changed the sign of the wrong number
changed both signs instead of one
items.why: Subtracting a number is adding its opposite. The opposite of −3 is 3, so 4 − (−3) = 4 + 3 = 7.

items.q: A freezer cools 2.5°C each minute. What is the change in temperature after 4 minutes?
misconceptions: ignored that cooling is a negative change
added 4 and 2.5 instead of multiplying
subtracted 4 from 2.5 instead of multiplying
correct
items.why: Cooling is a negative change, repeated 4 times: 4 × (−2.5) = −10. A positive number times a negative number is negative.
